- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (≥0.67) — apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model underestimates the drop — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >73), model fails to correct quickly — apply a “lag correction” by reducing forecast slope by 10–20% for the next 7–10 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >72 and true outcome is <70, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5 days; if <70 and true is >72, increase by 2–4%.
- Sentiment + price divergence: if sentiment is high (≥0.8) but price drops, model underreacts — add 1–2% upward bias to forecast for next 3 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overshoot early in the cycle — reduce forecast by 1–3% for days 1–5, then apply mean reversion logic for days 6–30.
